passage:
Santosh will do any dare. I've seen it. Last month Mohit said, 'Bet you can't jump off the pump-house roof,' and Santosh just did it, landed in the mud and laughed like it was a festival. He rode down the temple slope with no hands. He climbed the school gate at recess.
He never seems to think first. His eyes just go bright.
Then he twisted his wrist jumping off the wall behind the canteen. Our PT sir didn't shout. He took Santosh aside and said, 'No more roofs or walls. That's the rule. But you like adventure, so from Monday you're helping me set up the climbing rope for the sports team.'
Now Santosh is at the rope every lunch break, harness on, sir holding the line. He still grins the same way.
Gautam

qa.q: What did Santosh jump off after Mohit's dare?
qa.a: The pump-house roof.

qa.q: What do Santosh's bright eyes suggest about how he feels during a dare?
qa.a: They suggest he feels excited and thrilled, enjoying the moment without stopping to think about what could happen.

qa.q: What choice did the PT sir make after Santosh twisted his wrist?
qa.a: He set a firm rule of no more roofs or walls and gave Santosh a safe outlet, helping with the sports team's climbing rope.

qa.q: What would change if the PT sir had only shouted at Santosh?
qa.a: Santosh might have stopped for a while but kept looking for risky dares elsewhere, since the love of adventure would have no safe place to go.

grounding: Shows a child who takes dares and enjoys the thrill without thinking of consequences, and an adult who sets firm limits and offers a safe outlet.

passage:
Monday: Elizabeth's cousins dared her to jump from the high rock into the river, and she was in the air before anyone finished counting. Her aunt Salma came running, heart pounding, and pulled her out of the shallows by the arm. 'You didn't even look how deep it was!'
Wednesday: Aunt Salma drove her to the swimming pool in town. 'Jump here as much as you like. The lifeguard checks the depth. The river rock is off-limits, and that won't change.' Elizabeth jumped from the side eleven times, whooping.
Saturday: At the river again, a cousin said, 'Rock? Dare you.' Elizabeth looked at the rock, then at her aunt. 'Nah. Pool's better. You can do flips.'

qa.q: How many times did Elizabeth jump from the side of the pool?
qa.a: Eleven times, whooping.

qa.q: What was Aunt Salma feeling when she pulled Elizabeth out of the shallows?
qa.a: She was frightened, heart pounding, because Elizabeth had jumped without looking how deep the water was.

qa.q: What choice did Aunt Salma make on Wednesday, and why did it work?
qa.a: She took Elizabeth to the pool to jump freely while keeping the river rock firmly off-limits, giving the thrill a safe outlet with a clear limit.

qa.q: How might the cousins see Elizabeth turning down the dare on Saturday?
qa.a: They might be surprised, but her easy 'Pool's better' could make the risky dare seem less exciting to them too.

grounding: Shows a dare-loving child whose judgment is still developing, and an adult who gives a safe outlet for adventure along with a firm limit.

passage:
Saturday: Rafiq took a dare from the older boys and jumped off the colony's boundary wall. He landed hard, knees stinging, grinning wildly.
Sunday: He climbed halfway up the water-tank ladder before the watchman shouted. That evening his uncle Vijay heard about it and sat Rafiq down. "No more tank. Ever. That one's a firm no." Then Vijay added, "But you like the thrill, na? Let's find a good place for it."
The next Saturday: Vijay took him to the climbing wall at the sports complex. Harness on, helmet on, Rafiq reached the top twice and came down glowing. The older boys' dares didn't seem so interesting after that.

qa.q: What did Rafiq wear at the climbing wall?
qa.a: A harness and a helmet.

qa.q: How did Rafiq feel after jumping off the wall?
qa.a: He felt thrilled and proud, grinning wildly even with stinging knees.

qa.q: What did Vijay do that balanced safety and adventure?
qa.a: He set a firm limit about the tank the same evening and found a safe place for the thrill.

qa.q: How might the watchman have felt seeing Rafiq on the ladder?
qa.a: The watchman was probably alarmed and frightened for him, which is why he shouted.

grounding: Shows a dare-taking child and an adult who sets firm limits the same day and offers a safe outlet for adventure.

passage: When I was nine, in our village near Mangalore, I'd take any dare. Climb the cashew tree? Done. Jump into the pond from the high rock? Done, though I couldn't swim well. My friend Nitin would dare me and then cover his eyes. One day he dared me to cross the canal on the narrow pipe. I, Maria, was halfway across when I slipped and grabbed the edge. A fisherman pulled me out. That evening my grandmother didn't scold. She said, "You like the thrill? Fine. No pipes, no canals, never again. But on Sunday you come with me on the big boat." Out on the backwaters, holding the oar in the wind, I got all the thrill I wanted, safely.

qa.q: Who pulled young Maria out of the canal?
qa.a: A fisherman.

qa.q: How did young Maria feel about dares?
qa.a: Maria loved the thrill and felt fearless, taking any dare without thinking about what could happen.

qa.q: What was the turning point in the story?
qa.a: The slip on the pipe, after which the grandmother set a firm rule and offered the boat as a safe adventure.

qa.q: How might Nitin have felt watching the slip?
qa.a: Nitin was likely terrified and guilty, since he had given the dare.

grounding: Shows a thrill-seeking child who takes dares, and an elder who sets firm limits the same day and offers a safe adventure.

passage: The school picnic by the river had one rule, shouted twice by Afreen-ma'am: nobody goes past the red flags. But rain had made the rocks slippery and the water fast and brown, and the older boys dared Pranav to jump from the big rock into the pool beyond the flags. His heart raced. He was already climbing when a classmate ran to tell Afreen-ma'am. She was there in seconds. "Down. Now." Calm, but very firm. Pranav climbed down, cheeks hot. She didn't shame him in front of everyone. She walked him back inside the flags. "You love adventure. I can see that. So you lead the rope-bridge game after lunch. Anything past the flags, and you sit with me all day." Pranav grinned in spite of himself.

qa.q: What was the one rule at the picnic?
qa.a: Nobody goes past the red flags.

qa.q: How was Pranav feeling as he climbed the rock?
qa.a: He was excited and thrilled, his heart racing, without thinking about the fast water.

qa.q: What made Afreen-ma'am's response wise?
qa.a: She stopped the danger at once, set a firm limit without shaming him and gave him a safe adventure to lead.

qa.q: How might the classmate have felt running to tell Afreen-ma'am?
qa.a: The classmate was probably scared for Pranav and worried about seeming a tattletale, but chose his safety.

grounding: Illustrates a child tempted by a dangerous dare, with an adult giving a firm limit and a safe outlet for adventure.

passage:
"Bet you can't jump off the parking ramp onto the sand pile," Tejas said. The ramp in their Chennai building was taller than both of them.
Pradeep grinned. He loved dares. He'd already jumped the compound wall twice that week. He climbed onto the ramp's edge, heart racing with excitement.
"Pradeep! Down. Now." His father was coming back from the shop. Pradeep climbed down, cheeks hot.
Upstairs, his father didn't shout. "I know you love the thrill. But that height can break bones. Jumping off the ramp and the wall stops today. That's a firm rule."
Pradeep scowled. "It's boring then."
"So let's find a safe adventure. The sports complex has a climbing wall with ropes on Saturdays. I'll take you."
That evening his father also spoke to Tejas's mother. On Saturday, Pradeep reached the top of the climbing wall, whooping.

qa.q: What did Tejas dare Pradeep to do?
qa.a: To jump off the parking ramp onto the sand pile.

qa.q: How did Pradeep feel standing on the ramp's edge?
qa.a: He felt excited and thrilled, with his heart racing, enjoying the dare without thinking much about getting hurt.

qa.q: What did Pradeep's father do that protected him and still respected his love of adventure?
qa.a: He set a firm rule against jumping from the ramp and wall that same day, spoke to Tejas's mother, and offered the roped climbing wall as a safe outlet.

qa.q: How might Tejas's mother feel when Pradeep's father tells her about the dare?
qa.a: She might feel worried and glad to know, so she can talk to Tejas about dares that could hurt someone.

grounding: Shows a dare-loving child whose father sets a firm limit the same day and offers a safe outlet for adventure.
